headline: Election Commission Clerk Confesses He Accidentally Pasted 'Recipe for Aloo Gobi' Into Official Gazette
body:
Q: Mr. Sharma, can you explain exactly how a spice index ended up in the official notification intended for national oversight appointments?

A: Look, I was toggling between my Google Docs. My wife had sent me her grandmother’s secret tempering method for Aloo Gobi, and I was just trying to save it. My thumb slipped on the 'Ctrl+V' while I was supposed to be uploading the constitutional credentials. 

Q: And did you verify the document before pressing 'publish' on the government portal?

A: I did look at it, but I thought the bit about 'finely chopped ginger' was a coded reference to bureaucracy or maybe a very specific legislative metaphor. I just hit enter and went to grab my second chai of the morning.

Q: Now that the opposition is demanding an investigation into the 'mistake,' what do you plan to tell them?

A: I’m going to be honest. I’ll tell them it’s a failure of my kitchen-tech integration. If they want to cross-examine my sautéing technique, I’m ready. Honestly, the recipe is delicious, so maybe they should focus on the cumin seeds instead of the candidates.
caption: A clerical error of culinary proportions has left the nation's highest oversight body scrambling to explain a sudden surge in interest for Punjabi side dishes. Is it a mistake or a recipe for disaster? (satire) #Elections #AlooGobi #Governance
igHook: Would you trust a bureaucrat who can't distinguish between a constitutional oath and a potato curry recipe?
